neetpg2023-q001: Fever, arthralgia, a petechial rash and a low haemoglobin in a patient from Delhi during the monsoon, with thrombocytopenia, point to dengue. NS1 antigen is positive in the first 5 days and IgM thereafter.
neetpg2023-q002: Trichomonas vaginalis has only the trophozoite stage (no cyst), shows a characteristic jerky twitching motility on a wet saline mount, can be cultured (Diamond's medium, InPouch TV) and is sexually transmitted.
neetpg2023-q003: An ulcer on the leg in a patient from West Rajasthan (a desert zone) with amastigotes showing nucleus and kinetoplast is cutaneous leishmaniasis, caused by Leishmania tropica. Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is due to L. donovani.
neetpg2023-q004: A child with a rash and fever, and urine cells with owl's eye inclusions (large intranuclear inclusion with a halo), has cytomegalovirus infection. Owl's eye cells are seen in urine cytology.
neetpg2023-q005: Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini, the liver flukes, are associated with cholangiocarcinoma. Schistosoma haematobium is associated with bladder cancer.
neetpg2023-q006: A poorly adherent HIV patient with persistent cough and weight loss is most likely to have an opportunistic pulmonary infection. The key marks Pneumocystis jirovecii, which causes pneumonia with dry cough when the CD4 count falls below 200.
neetpg2023-q007: Fever, jaundice, conjunctival suffusion and haematuria in a sewage worker is leptospirosis (Weil disease). The microscopic agglutination test (MAT) is the gold standard serological test.
neetpg2023-q008: Rotavirus gastroenteritis is diagnosed by detection of viral antigen in stool by ELISA or latex agglutination. It is also detected by RT-PCR.
neetpg2023-q009: Histidine-rich protein 2 (HRP-2) is an antigen specific to Plasmodium falciparum, detected by rapid diagnostic tests. LDH-based tests detect other species.
neetpg2023-q010: A child with meningitis whose CSF shows pleomorphic Gram-negative coccobacilli is infected with Haemophilus influenzae. It shows satellitism around Staphylococcus aureus because it needs factor V (NAD) and factor X (haemin).
neetpg2023-q011: Intracellular Gram-negative diplococci in a urethral discharge are Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Treatment is ceftriaxone (usually with azithromycin or doxycycline for Chlamydia).
neetpg2023-q012: A swelling over the parietal bone since birth that does not cross suture lines and is seen on X-ray as a subperiosteal collection is a cephalhaematoma. Caput succedaneum crosses suture lines, and subgaleal haematoma spreads widely.
neetpg2023-q013: A small, shrunken, calcified non-functioning kidney in a patient with sterile pyuria is putty kidney (autonephrectomy), a late complication of renal tuberculosis.
neetpg2023-q014: A defect of the fascia transversalis (the marked structure, the deep inguinal ring or its posterior wall) is the cause of inguinal hernias. The deep inguinal ring is an opening in the fascia transversalis.
neetpg2023-q015: The lateral pterygoid muscle is attached to the articular disc and the neck of the mandible. In yawning it pulls the disc forwards, and a locked jaw (dislocation) results. It is the only masticatory muscle that opens the mouth.
neetpg2023-q016: A renal corpuscle seen as a tuft of capillaries (glomerulus) surrounded by a Bowman capsule with a urinary space, with proximal and distal tubules around it, is a glomerulus.
neetpg2023-q017: The shown defect (coarctation or a persistent ductus arteriosus-type defect of the aortic arch) is due to the left sixth arch, from which the ductus arteriosus forms on the left. The right 4th arch gives the right subclavian artery, and the left 4th gives the aortic arch.
neetpg2023-q018: The median umbilical ligament is the remnant of the urachus (allantois), which connects the bladder apex to the umbilicus. The medial umbilical ligaments are the obliterated umbilical arteries and the ligamentum teres is the obliterated umbilical vein.
neetpg2023-q019: In portal hypertension a portosystemic anastomosis forms at the lower end of the oesophagus between the oesophageal veins (systemic, to azygos) and the left gastric vein (portal), producing oesophageal varices.
neetpg2023-q020: Gamma-glutamyl carboxylase carboxylates glutamate residues of the vitamin K dependent factors II, VII, IX and X (and proteins C and S), which allows them to bind calcium. Warfarin blocks this.
neetpg2023-q021: Diarrhoea, dermatitis and dementia describe pellagra, due to niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency, common in maize eaters and carcinoid syndrome. Hartnup disease is another cause.
neetpg2023-q022: Exercise-induced cramps with relief on rest in a boy, with a second-wind phenomenon, indicates McArdle disease (type V glycogen storage disease), with muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency. Hypoglycaemia is not typical of McArdle, but the key marks it.
neetpg2023-q023: A family eating only polished rice (the thiamine-rich husk is removed) develops thiamine deficiency (beriberi). Erythrocyte transketolase activity is reduced and used as a diagnostic test.
neetpg2023-q024: Confusion, ataxia and painful eye movements (ophthalmoplegia) in an alcoholic is Wernicke encephalopathy, caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency. It is treated with IV thiamine before glucose.
neetpg2023-q025: Fasting hypoglycaemia with absent liver glycogen suggests glycogen synthase deficiency (type 0 glycogen storage disease), where glycogen cannot be made. Blood glucose rises little after meals, and ketosis develops after fasting.
neetpg2023-q026: Pedal oedema with cardiomegaly in a child (wet beriberi) is due to thiamine deficiency. Cheilosis suggests riboflavin deficiency, but the cardiac features point to thiamine.
neetpg2023-q027: Alcohol metabolism raises NADH/NAD+, which converts pyruvate to lactate, so lactic acidosis occurs. Lactate competes with urate for excretion in the kidney, and so urate rises, precipitating gout.
neetpg2023-q028: Perioral and acral erythematous scaly patches with delayed wound healing in a child suggest zinc deficiency (acrodermatitis enteropathica, due to a SLC39A4 mutation). Treatment is oral zinc.
neetpg2023-q029: Vitamin C is a cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase in collagen synthesis. Deficiency causes defective collagen, leading to bleeding gums, perifollicular haemorrhages and corkscrew hairs (scurvy).
neetpg2023-q030: A low insulin to glucagon ratio (fasting) activates hormone-sensitive lipase, causing lipolysis, and also glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis. Lipoprotein lipase, glycogen synthase and PFK-1 are activated when insulin is high.
neetpg2023-q031: Urine that turns black on standing, due to oxidation of homogentisic acid, is characteristic of alkaptonuria. Ochronosis and arthritis develop later in life.
neetpg2023-q032: Raw egg white contains avidin, which binds biotin and prevents its absorption. Biotin deficiency causes alopecia, scaly dermatitis and neurological symptoms.
neetpg2023-q033: A child with developmental regression and a cherry-red spot on the macula without hepatosplenomegaly has Tay-Sachs disease (hexosaminidase A deficiency). Niemann-Pick disease has organomegaly.
neetpg2023-q034: Right homonymous hemianopia (loss of the right half of both visual fields) is caused by a lesion of the left optic tract, left optic radiation or left occipital cortex. The key marks the left optic tract.
neetpg2023-q035: A diabetic woman with painless gradual visual loss and a greyish, opacified lens has an immature senile cataract, treated with phacoemulsification and an intraocular lens, with control of diabetes.
neetpg2023-q036: A solid, yellowish nodule on the sclera near the limbus in a young child (from birth) is a limbal dermoid, a choristoma containing skin elements. Dermolipoma is more fleshy and lies at the outer canthus.
neetpg2023-q037: A golden-brown ring at the corneal periphery (Kayser-Fleischer ring) suggests Wilson disease. The next test is serum ceruloplasmin (low), with 24-hour urinary copper.
neetpg2023-q038: Fluorescein dye stains corneal epithelial defects and ulcers green. It is viewed under a cobalt blue filter. Lissamine green stains dead or devitalised cells.
neetpg2023-q039: Verrucous carcinoma of the glans with no palpable nodes is locally invasive with a low metastatic potential. The key advises partial penectomy, a penis-preserving approach being considered for small lesions.
neetpg2023-q040: A needle driven into the proximal tibia with the child's leg stabilised shows intraosseous access, used to give IV fluids and drugs in emergencies when peripheral veins can't be accessed.
neetpg2023-q041: Sudden onset of perineal pain, foul-smelling discharge and necrotic tissue in a diabetic is Fournier's gangrene, a polymicrobial (aerobic and anaerobic) necrotising fasciitis. It needs early surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics.
neetpg2023-q042: Ligation of the inferior mesenteric artery near its origin during abdominoperineal resection can injure the superior hypogastric plexus (sympathetic) and cause retrograde ejaculation and bladder dysfunction. Pelvic parasympathetic (nervi erigentes) injury causes impotence.
neetpg2023-q043: A firm, raised scar that extends beyond the original wound margins, appearing after a chest injury a year earlier, is a keloid. A hypertrophic scar stays within the wound margins and regresses.
neetpg2023-q044: Pain and numbness over the anterolateral thigh after laparoscopic hernia repair is meralgia paraesthetica, from entrapment of the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh by tacks or staples, in the triangle of pain.
neetpg2023-q045: Eye opening to pain gives E2, inappropriate words gives V3 and withdrawal to pain gives M4, i.e. E2V3M4, a GCS of 9.
neetpg2023-q046: Fever, abdominal pain and jaundice with a cystic liver lesion having daughter cysts is a hydatid cyst of the liver, from Echinococcus granulosus. FNAC is contraindicated because of the risk of spillage and anaphylaxis.
neetpg2023-q047: Unintentional weight loss in a chronic alcoholic with raised ALP and a rising AFP suggests hepatocellular carcinoma. Alcoholic hepatitis has AST/ALT above 2.
neetpg2023-q048: p-Phenylenediamine (PPD) in hair dye is a common cause of allergic contact dermatitis, which can be severe with face swelling. Patch testing confirms it.
neetpg2023-q049: Acne that does not respond to isotretinoin and antibiotics in a woman should prompt evaluation for hyperandrogenism, such as PCOS or congenital adrenal hyperplasia (testosterone, DHEAS, LH/FSH).
neetpg2023-q050: The head tilt-chin lift manoeuvre opens the airway by lifting the tongue off the back of the pharynx. When cervical spine injury is suspected, jaw thrust is used instead.
neetpg2023-q051: In chronic pancreatitis with a dilated main duct (above 7 mm) and intraductal stones, the surgery of choice is longitudinal (lateral) pancreaticojejunostomy, the Puestow or Partington-Rochelle procedure, which decompresses the duct. A head mass needs a Whipple or Beger procedure.
neetpg2023-q052: A painless genital ulcer (chancre) with non-tender, rubbery inguinal lymphadenopathy is primary syphilis. Chancroid is painful, with tender suppurative nodes.
neetpg2023-q053: Ocular melanocytosis (oculodermal melanocytosis or nevus of Ota) shows bluish-grey pigmentation of the sclera and periocular skin. It is associated with glaucoma and uveal malignant melanoma, and the key marks malignant melanoma.
neetpg2023-q054: Cefazolin, a first-generation cephalosporin, is the antibiotic of choice for surgical prophylaxis in cardiac surgery, given within 60 minutes before the incision. Vancomycin is added if MRSA risk is high.
neetpg2023-q055: Non-axial proptosis in a patient with a previous head injury 15 years ago and an opacified frontal sinus on CT suggests a frontal mucocele, from obstruction of the sinus ostium after trauma. The mucocele expands and pushes the orbit downwards and laterally.
neetpg2023-q056: Oestrogen receptor (ER) positivity is a good prognostic factor in breast cancer because the tumour responds to hormonal therapy. BRCA-1, p53 and high Ki-67 (proliferation) all indicate worse outcomes.
neetpg2023-q057: A neck stoma (permanent opening in the front of the neck) after surgery for laryngeal cancer shows a total laryngectomy, in which the airway is separated from the pharynx. Tracheostomy preserves the larynx.
neetpg2023-q058: Sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the interscapular region, a widened mediastinum and a blood pressure difference between the arms is acute aortic dissection. A CT angiogram or TEE confirms it.
neetpg2023-q059: A Rinne test negative at 256 and 512 Hz but positive at 1024 Hz indicates an air-bone gap of about 30-45 dB. Rinne is negative at 256 Hz for a gap of 15-30 dB or more, and at 512 Hz for a gap of 30-45 dB (in the standard rule), and at 1024 Hz for 45 dB and above.
neetpg2023-q060: A small amoebic liver abscess (under 5 cm; about 25 mL here) after a diarrhoeal illness responds to metronidazole, so it is treated medically. Aspiration is reserved for large (above 10 cm), left lobe, or non-responding abscesses.
neetpg2023-q061: The radiograph shows widened, cupped metaphyses with bowing deformities, the features of rickets, from vitamin D deficiency.
neetpg2023-q062: A patient with trauma a week back who becomes confused and ataxic with a crescent-shaped, concave hyperdense collection on CT has a subdural haemorrhage. Chronic alcohol users and the elderly have fragile bridging veins.
neetpg2023-q063: Necrotising fasciitis is a rapidly spreading infection with fascial necrosis. It needs urgent radical debridement (repeated every 24 hours if needed), antibiotics, and hyperbaric oxygen may be used as an adjunct. The false statement is that hyperbaric oxygen has no role.
neetpg2023-q064: Oral thrush (white patches on the tongue and buccal mucosa) in an asthmatic using inhaled steroids is oral candidiasis. It is treated with topical clotrimazole or nystatin. Griseofulvin and terbinafine do not act on Candida.
neetpg2023-q065: A direct inguinal hernia passes through Hesselbach's triangle, due to weakness of the posterior wall of the inguinal canal formed by the conjoint tendon and transversalis fascia.
neetpg2023-q066: Carboprost (15-methyl prostaglandin F2 alpha) can cause bronchospasm and is contraindicated in asthma. Oxytocin is the first-line uterotonic and is safe, and methylergometrine is avoided in hypertension.
neetpg2023-q067: The splint shown (cock-up wrist splint) is used for radial nerve palsy, which causes wrist drop. It keeps the wrist extended while the nerve recovers.
neetpg2023-q068: Omapatrilat inhibits both angiotensin-converting enzyme and neutral endopeptidase (vasopeptidase inhibitor). It was withdrawn for angioedema. Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin only.
neetpg2023-q069: Chronic knee pain without trauma, with a smooth-bordered separate fragment at the superolateral corner on a radiograph, is a bipartite patella (a normal variant, often bilateral). Check the other knee for the same finding, and no fixation is needed.
neetpg2023-q070: Vibration-induced white finger (Raynaud's phenomenon of occupational origin) is caused by exposure to vibrating tools such as pneumatic drills.
neetpg2023-q071: Fatigue, dyspnoea and weight gain in a patient on amiodarone suggest amiodarone-induced hypothyroidism (also pulmonary fibrosis). Amiodarone is rich in iodine and inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to T3.
neetpg2023-q072: Juvenile (retention) polyps in a young child, with cystically dilated glands filled with mucin and inflammation, present with painless rectal bleeding and prolapse. They are hamartomas, with no malignant potential when solitary.
neetpg2023-q073: Aspirin (salicylate) overdose is treated with IV sodium bicarbonate, which alkalinises the urine and enhances salicylate excretion, plus activated charcoal. N-acetylcysteine is for paracetamol, and haemodialysis is for severe cases.
neetpg2023-q074: Abrupt stopping of clonidine causes rebound hypertension with headache, due to a surge in sympathetic activity as alpha 2 receptor stimulation is withdrawn. It is prevented by tapering.
neetpg2023-q075: A punched-out, painless ulcer on the sole of the foot with surrounding callus in a neuropathic limb is a trophic (neuropathic) ulcer, as in diabetes or leprosy.
neetpg2023-q076: Allopurinol is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor and so inhibits the synthesis of uric acid. Probenecid is uricosuric, and colchicine and NSAIDs treat acute attacks.
neetpg2023-q077: Oprelvekin (recombinant IL-11) stimulates megakaryocyte production and is used to treat chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Filgrastim treats neutropenia and erythropoietin treats anaemia.
neetpg2023-q078: Losartan has a uricosuric effect and also blocks thromboxane A2 receptors. This makes it the only ARB useful in gout. The statement about losartan acting as a thromboxane antagonist is the true one.
neetpg2023-q079: Night-time numbness and tingling in the lateral three and a half digits, relieved by shaking the hands (flick sign), is carpal tunnel syndrome. Durkan's carpal compression test is positive. Phalen's and Tinel's signs are also used.
neetpg2023-q080: A child with a lower limb deformity, hyperpigmented skin lesions (café-au-lait spots) and a 'shepherd's crook' deformity of the femur with ground-glass bone is fibrous dysplasia (McCune-Albright syndrome).
neetpg2023-q081: A treatment-resistant schizophrenic patient who develops hypersalivation, hyperglycaemia and dyslipidaemia is on clozapine. It is used after failure of two antipsychotics and needs monitoring of the blood counts for agranulocytosis.
neetpg2023-q082: A young adult with an eccentric, lytic, expansile lesion at the epiphysis of a long bone with a soap-bubble appearance is a giant cell tumour (osteoclastoma).
neetpg2023-q083: Functional residual capacity is the volume left in the lungs after a normal expiration (expiratory reserve volume plus residual volume). In the spirogram it is the area at the end of a quiet expiration.
neetpg2023-q084: In the CEAP classification, C4a is pigmentation or eczema, C4b is lipodermatosclerosis or atrophie blanche, C3 is oedema, C5 is a healed ulcer and C6 is an active ulcer. Eczema is therefore C4a.
neetpg2023-q085: A subarachnoid haemorrhage on CT is next investigated by CT or digital subtraction angiography to find the aneurysm. Nimodipine is given to prevent vasospasm, and the key marks angiography.
neetpg2023-q086: Heat stroke presents with a very high temperature, hot dry skin with no sweating, tachypnoea, hypotension and altered sensorium. Sweating is not a feature of classic heat stroke, hence it is the exception.
neetpg2023-q087: In a renal clearance graph, PAH clearance is the highest (it measures renal plasma flow), inulin clearance equals GFR (about 125 mL/min), glucose clearance is zero at normal plasma concentrations, and bicarbonate is close to zero. The matching shown is glucose, bicarbonate, inulin and PAH.
neetpg2023-q088: After a corrosive (sodium hydroxide) ingestion with complete dysphagia, a feeding jejunostomy is done to bypass the injured oesophagus and give nutrition, before the strictures are managed. Early endoscopy is done within 24 hours.
neetpg2023-q089: A midline neck swelling that moves with swallowing and also on protrusion of the tongue is a thyroglossal cyst. It moves with the tongue because it is attached to the hyoid and foramen caecum by the thyroglossal duct.
neetpg2023-q090: In a nerve action potential curve the period from the start of the spike to the end of repolarisation is the absolute and relative refractory period, when a second stimulus can't (or only strongly) trigger an action potential. The threshold is where depolarisation starts.
neetpg2023-q091: The qSOFA score uses systolic blood pressure of 100 mmHg or less, respiratory rate of 22 or more per minute and altered mentation (GCS below 15). A score of 2 or more suggests sepsis in the bedside screening.
neetpg2023-q092: Facilitated diffusion uses a carrier or channel protein to move a substance down its concentration gradient without energy. It is saturable and specific, unlike simple diffusion.
neetpg2023-q093: A pansystolic murmur radiating to the axilla is mitral regurgitation. The shown murmur waveform is holosystolic.
neetpg2023-q094: Tearfulness, mood swings and insomnia starting a few days after delivery and settling within two weeks are postpartum (maternity) blues, requiring only reassurance and support.
neetpg2023-q095: Recurrent episodes of sudden anxiety with palpitations, sweating, breathlessness, chest pain and a feeling of impending doom, peaking within minutes, is panic disorder. Generalised anxiety disorder is a persistent, continuous worry.
neetpg2023-q096: Inflammatory back pain with morning stiffness that improves with exercise, red eyes (uveitis) and reduced chest expansion is ankylosing spondylitis, with bamboo spine and sacroiliitis on X-ray.
neetpg2023-q097: Drowsiness and seizures towards the end of dialysis are dialysis disequilibrium syndrome, from cerebral oedema as urea is removed faster from blood than from the brain. IV mannitol (or hypertonic saline) reduces the oedema.
neetpg2023-q098: Restlessness, palpitations, tremor and a swollen neck suggest thyroid storm. A beta blocker such as propranolol is contraindicated in asthma, so a calcium channel blocker (diltiazem) is used to control the heart rate, along with propylthiouracil, iodine and steroids.
neetpg2023-q099: In neonatal respiratory distress syndrome, surfactant is deficient. This raises alveolar surface tension, so the lungs become stiff and compliance falls.
neetpg2023-q100: The squeeze technique (and the stop-start technique) are behavioural methods for premature ejaculation. The squeeze technique involves pressing the glans before the point of ejaculation. SSRIs such as dapoxetine are the drug options.
neetpg2023-q101: HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B with a viral load above 20,000 IU/mL and ALT above twice the normal limit needs antiviral therapy. Tenofovir or entecavir (high barrier to resistance) are preferred, for a long and often indefinite course. The key marks tenofovir.
neetpg2023-q102: Palpitations, sweating, restlessness, sweaty palms and ophthalmopathy in a young adult indicate Graves disease. It is caused by thyroid receptor (TSH receptor) stimulating antibodies, and TSH is suppressed.
neetpg2023-q103: Painless violaceous or purple nodular skin lesions in an HIV-positive patient are Kaposi sarcoma, caused by HHV-8. It is an AIDS-defining illness.
neetpg2023-q104: Raising extracellular potassium (hyperkalaemia, e.g. 5.5 mEq/L) reduces the potassium gradient, so the resting membrane potential becomes less negative (more positive), moving closer to threshold.
neetpg2023-q105: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome is caused by deficiency of surfactant, whose main component is dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (lecithin). The L:S ratio of 2 or more shows lung maturity.
neetpg2023-q106: Resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia and reduced emotional expression (masked facies) are features of Parkinson's disease, due to degeneration of dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra in the basal ganglia.
neetpg2023-q107: Umbilicated papules and nodules on the face and trunk with cough and weight loss in an HIV-positive man may be disseminated histoplasmosis or cryptococcosis. The key marks histoplasmosis. Molluscum contagiosum also causes umbilicated papules but does not explain the cough.
neetpg2023-q108: Fibres of the fasciculus gracilis (lower limb) lie medial and fasciculus cuneatus (upper limb) lie lateral in the dorsal column. A lesion of the lateral part therefore affects ipsilateral arm proprioception.
neetpg2023-q109: Seizures, fever, headache and confusion with bitemporal lobe inflammation on MRI is herpes simplex encephalitis. It is treated with IV acyclovir at once, and PCR on CSF confirms.
neetpg2023-q110: The plateau phase (phase 2) of the myocardial action potential is due to slow, prolonged opening of L-type calcium channels, balanced by outward potassium current. It makes the cardiac refractory period long.
neetpg2023-q111: Loss of proprioception and vibration with upper motor neuron signs and angular stomatitis (suggesting B12 deficiency) is subacute combined degeneration of the cord, affecting the dorsal columns and the lateral corticospinal tracts.
neetpg2023-q112: In severe dehydration the initial step is airway, breathing and circulation, with normal saline 20 mL/kg bolus. Insulin is started only after rehydration (after 1-2 hours) because insulin can drop potassium.
neetpg2023-q113: A healthy infant gains about 25 cm in length in the first year. The weight roughly doubles by 5 months and triples by 1 year. The fontanelle closes by 12-18 months.
neetpg2023-q114: A mid-diastolic murmur with a prominent a wave in the JVP is tricuspid stenosis, with forceful right atrial contraction against a stenosed tricuspid valve.
neetpg2023-q115: Deafness, cataract and patent ductus arteriosus is the classic triad of congenital rubella syndrome (Gregg's triad). The blueberry muffin rash is also seen.
neetpg2023-q116: In poor farmers of a village consuming rice and pulses (Lathyrus sativus), spastic paraparesis with crossed gait is lathyrism, caused by the neurotoxin beta-oxalyl-amino-alanine (BOAA, ODAP). The key lists vitamin C, which looks doubtful.
neetpg2023-q117: Workers exposed to aniline dye for more than 20 years are identified from past records and followed through to the present for bladder cancer, a retrospective (historical) cohort study. The exposure and outcome have already occurred.
neetpg2023-q118: A raised sweat chloride concentration (above 60 mmol/L) on pilocarpine iontophoresis is the diagnostic test for cystic fibrosis.
neetpg2023-q119: Fever, a maculopapular rash starting behind the ears and face, and Koplik's spots on the buccal mucosa are pathognomonic of measles.
neetpg2023-q120: Blood pressure tracking means individuals tend to keep their relative BP position (percentile) from childhood to adulthood. Those with low BP as children remain low.
neetpg2023-q121: Paroxysmal cough with apnoea in a young infant and a very high lymphocyte count (above 50,000/microL) is pertussis. Azithromycin is the drug of choice in infants under 1 month, as erythromycin is linked to pyloric stenosis.
neetpg2023-q122: The Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) is the village-level health worker who counsels women on nutrition and links them with the health system. Night blindness in pregnancy is vitamin A deficiency.
neetpg2023-q123: The fossa of Rosenmuller (pharyngeal recess) is a depression behind the torus tubarius in the nasopharynx. It is a common site of origin for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
neetpg2023-q124: Under the NACO syndromic approach, kit 2 (grey) is for cervicitis (cervical discharge or erosions): azithromycin 1 g and cefixime 400 mg. Kit 1 (white) is for urethral discharge, kit 3 (green) for vaginal discharge and kit 4 (red) for genital ulcer.
neetpg2023-q125: Years of potential life lost (YPLL) measures premature mortality, i.e. the years lost because death occurred before a reference age (usually 65 or 70).
neetpg2023-q126: The instrument shown is a tracheostomy tube, used for airway toilet, acute upper airway obstruction and prolonged ventilation. It is not used for examining the upper airway.
neetpg2023-q127: At 10 years of age, the Universal Immunisation Programme gives TT/Td. Measles, rotavirus and hepatitis B are infant vaccines.
neetpg2023-q128: Ear pain with tonsillitis is referred otalgia through the tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve (Jacobson's nerve), which supplies both the tonsil and the middle ear.
neetpg2023-q129: The Colombo Plan, under which cobalt-60 teletherapy units were installed in India, was a programme of help for radiotherapy facilities in cancer treatment.
neetpg2023-q130: Progressive spastic paraparesis in poor farmers after crop failure and diets with Lathyrus sativus (khesari dal) is lathyrism, due to the neurotoxin beta-oxalyl-amino-alanine (BOAA or beta-ODAP).
neetpg2023-q131: For a clean minor wound in a patient who received a full tetanus course more than 5 years ago (10 years here), a single booster dose of tetanus toxoid is given. Immunoglobulin is not needed.
neetpg2023-q132: For bacteriological water sampling, the tap is flamed or cleaned, water is run for 1-2 minutes, and the sample is collected in a sterile bottle in a gentle stream, taking care not to touch the tap, to avoid spillage and contamination.
neetpg2023-q133: Fever, headache and a pleomorphic rash (lesions at different stages) that spares the palms and soles is chickenpox. Isolation until all lesions have crusted (about 6 days after the onset of the rash) is the next step.
neetpg2023-q134: The ECG shows peaked T waves from hyperkalaemia, a recognised effect of spironolactone (a potassium-sparing diuretic), particularly with ACE inhibitors or ARBs. Hydrochlorothiazide causes hypokalaemia.
neetpg2023-q135: A 78-year-old with progressive decline, visual hallucinations and parkinsonism fits Lewy body dementia, though the key marks Parkinson's disease (dementia in Parkinson's disease). The timing of cognitive decline relative to motor symptoms separates the two.
neetpg2023-q136: After hypophysectomy, central diabetes insipidus (dilute urine with high sodium) is treated with desmopressin (DDAVP) supplements. Since the posterior pituitary is removed, the replacement is lifelong.
neetpg2023-q137: Upper chest discomfort, ptosis (Horner syndrome) and pain radiating to the upper limb in a heavy smoker point to a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour) compressing the sympathetic chain and the brachial plexus.
neetpg2023-q138: Acute painful swelling of the first metatarsophalangeal joint in a heavy drinker with raised uric acid and negatively birefringent needle crystals is acute gout. Alcohol raises urate.
neetpg2023-q139: Confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia (here with sixth nerve palsy) in a chronic alcoholic is Wernicke's encephalopathy, caused by thiamine deficiency. Treat with IV thiamine before glucose.
neetpg2023-q140: A serum level of 4 against a target of 1 needs two half-lives to fall to 1 (4 to 2 to 1). With a half-life of 40 hours, this takes 80 hours.
neetpg2023-q141: A sudden rise in temperature (with flushing, dry skin and tachycardia) after atropine in an organophosphate poisoning patient is atropine toxicity. The dose is titrated to reach atropinisation (dry chest), not beyond.
neetpg2023-q142: The partogram shows arrest of cervical dilatation with the alert and action lines crossed, despite oxytocin. This is arrest of labour, usually due to cephalopelvic disproportion, and requires a caesarean section.
